title: Stuffed Tomato with Rice and Meat

content.title: About
content.content: Stuffed tomato with rice and meat is a classic dish consisting of a ripe tomato filled with a mixture of boiled rice, ground meat (usually beef or pork), onion and spices. The tomato is baked until tender, resulting in a fragrant and hearty meal.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The dish is popular in Mediterranean, Balkan and Middle Eastern cuisines.
Traditionally the tomato interior is scooped out and the flesh is used in sauces or soups.
Some regional versions add pine nuts or raisins for a subtle sweet note.
Stuffed tomatoes are often served as part of festive tables or family lunches.
A lighter version replaces meat with chicken or turkey.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Meat and rice provide B12, B6 and niacin, which support metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Good source of protein
items.content: Ground beef or pork supplies complete animal protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Lycopene in tomatoes
items.content: Tomatoes are high in lycopene, a powerful antioxidant that promotes heart health and may reduce the risk of certain cancers.

items.title: Complex carbohydrates
items.content: Rice offers slow‑releasing energy, helping to maintain satiety.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: The dish contains iron, zinc and potassium, important for blood formation, immunity and blood‑pressure regulation.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Using ready‑made sauces or adding excess salt can make the dish too salty, which is undesirable for hypertension.

items.title: Meat fat content
items.content: Fatty cuts of beef or pork increase calories and saturated fat; choosing lean cuts is recommended.

items.title: Tomato allergy
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to tomatoes, experiencing skin rashes or food‑related reactions.

items.title: Thorough cooking required
items.content: Undercooked ground meat may harbor pathogens; ensure the internal temperature reaches at least 71 °C.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the stuffed tomato hot, often accompanied by a fresh vegetable side, yogurt‑based sauce, or a green salad. It can be enjoyed as a main course or as part of a larger meal.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Cooked stuffed tomatoes keep in the refrigerator in an airtight container for up to 3 days. For longer storage, freeze in portion‑size bags for up to 2 months. Reheat thoroughly before serving.
